description: A group of life long learners
details: Simba is a health monitor for astronauts that shows their body as an interactive 3D model, coloured by live vitals. Readings such as heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, temperature, radiation dose and bone density are pinned to the matching spot on the body. Normal readings stay out of the way, while anything abnormal glows, pulses and raises an alert. Normal ranges change with the mission (ISS, lunar surface, Mars transit or Mars surface), so the same reading can be fine on the Moon but a warning in orbit. Astronauts can also photograph a rash, bruise or swelling, tag it to a body area and keep a log. Everything works on the device without a ground link.
